Senior Half-Recital

Each student desiring to pursue a music major at WSU must have an audition with the studio teacher of the major instrument or voice of intended study, and in the case of multiple teachers in the studio, with the area coordinator. Faculty and students are encouraged to set up an audition before the semester, use the first lesson as an audition, or use the ensemble placement audition as the audition. 

To be admitted as a major pursuing any Bachelor of Music degree, students must meet the following criteria:

1. Successfully audition into 300-level lessons on their major instrument or voice.
  
2. Enroll in MUS 251 and 252 or be approved to receive transfer credit by the Music Theory Area Coordinator. 

In addition, for students advancing in any of the Bachelor of Music Education degrees, the College of Education, Sport, and Human Sciences requires 2.5 GPA and C or better in each course listed for the major, minor and professional core, plus a 2.5 cumulative GPA.

Students following any teacher preparation option are required to present an acceptable senior half recital in the major performance medium. 

Students following any teacher preparation option must have a minimum GPA of 2.5 in all of the following areas: cumulative GPA, Professional Education Core with a C or better in each course, and academic major (and minor if any) with a C or better in each course. Students must also be admitted into the College of Education, Sport, and Human Sciences. Since this option is likely to lead to enrollment in the MA in Music, students are advised that admission to graduate study requires a 3.0 cumulative GPA.

Requirements include: pass the piano proficiency exam, second-year assessment, achieve a cumulative 2.5 GPA and a grade of C or better in all music classes, and a 2.5 GPA and a grade of C or better in all College of Education, Sport, and Human Sciences Professional Core courses. Class piano credits are not required for the degree.

This option provides professional preparation in music combined with studies in education.  Students may complete teacher certification requirements after completion of this degree through further enrollment as undergraduate second degree candidates, enrollment as post-baccalaureate non-degree students, or as graduate students, each of which requires application for admission.  Students planning to seek admission and enroll as graduate students should, at the beginning of their last semester of undergraduate study, complete the necessary form to count selected courses in the final undergraduate semester toward the graduate degree, up to a maximum of 6 credits. Note that during the second term of the senior year, only 10 credits are taken toward the degree. Students must enroll in 12 credits to be full time and may enroll in graduate credits if preparing to enroll in the MA degree program. Please see your advisor for additional details and recommendations.  

If a student elects to pursue teacher certification in choral music, instrumental music, or general music, requirements include in addition to those listed above, 4 credits of vocal lessons and/or ensembles for instrumentalists or 4 credits of instrumental lessons and/or ensembles for vocalists.

A minimum of 1 music ensemble credit is required during each of 7 semesters, to include at least one semester of MUS 435 for instrumentalists and MUS 428 or MUS 433 for vocalists. Must include a minimum of 2 credits in choral and 2 credits in instrumental performing groups. 

Only 9 credits of MUS courses can be used to fulfill UCORE requirements.
